local_first_answer: Generation, browser sanity checks and optional OCR/PDF extraction can run in the user's browser on the user's hardware. GitHub Pages is static hosting only and no application server is required for the default workflow. Official KoSIT/Mustang/veraPDF validation is currently best handled as a local CLI/Desktop step, not as a remote server upload.

invoice_converter_com.observed_positioning: Competitor positions around upload -> extraction/review -> standards-aligned download for XRechnung, ZUGFeRD, Factur-X, UBL and CII. Our differentiation remains local-first/no-server-upload.

pdf24.observed_from_search: PDF24 offers online and offline e-invoice creation flows. Useful UX reference: start from a document/form, fill required invoice data, export e-invoice, but keep our product local-first and honest about validation.

current_limits: CLI xrechnung-ubl now has a minimal JSON example that passes local KoSIT validation, but broader field coverage still needs iterative hardening.

Browser app runs generation and sanity validation on the user's hardware, but does not yet ship KoSIT as a pure Browser/WebAssembly runtime; official validation uses local CLI/native validator artifacts.

Browser app parses TXT/CSV/XML locally and has a reviewed hook for PDF/DOC/DOCX local extraction. PDF.js is selected for the next embedded-text PDF spike, but it is not shipped yet; scanned PDFs still need a separate local OCR engine and every extracted field stays human-review-gated.
